text:
Ilya Sorokin faced 50 shots on Saturday and stopped 45 of them, including a Jack Hughes chance early in overtime that our win probability model rated the biggest save of the night. Twenty seconds later Hughes got another one, a breakaway at 1:18, and the Devils had come back from 4-2 down to win 5-4 at UBS Arena. New Jersey has won four straight.

The Islanders led for most of the night, and on the scoreboard they earned that lead. Anthony Duclair and Evan Rodrigues traded goals 17 seconds apart late in the first, and rookie Matthew Schaefer put New York back in front at 17:14. Declan Chisholm tied it on a 5 percent shot early in the second, Simon Holmstrom answered 26 seconds later, and Victor Eklund poked one in at 11:54 to make it 4-2.

But the shot clock had been tilting all night, and in the third it tipped over. The Devils out-chanced New York 2.02 to 1.07 in expected goals (the quality of chances) in the period. Luke Evangelista batted one in at 6:08, and Dougie Hamilton tied it on a power play at 13:42, a goal that took New Jersey from 20 percent to 54. By the end the Devils had 81 shot attempts to 44, 5.45 expected goals to 3.24, and by our numbers they deserved to win 80 percent of the time. Sorokin, about half a goal better than expected, was the only reason this went past regulation.

The night had an edge to it. Schaefer and Luke Hughes traded punches, the kind of scrap between two young cornerstone defensemen that tends to get replayed, and the Islanders took 32 penalty minutes to New Jersey's four. In overtime Schaefer went down without a call, and afterward, as NHL.com's Stefen Rosner posted, he said: "I thought I [got tripped], but I mean, they could have seen otherwise."

The Devils got 19 saves from Jake Allen on 23 shots, a bit below what the chances deserved, and it didn't matter. This was their third straight game to overtime, they keep generating offense in waves, and the Maple Leafs are next. The Islanders, already without Ryan Pulock, lost a game they led by two and were outshot 50 to 23.
headline: Devils pour 50 shots on Sorokin, Hughes ends it
